title: Compatibility decision log and publish workflow
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a lightweight decision log for compatibility judgments and the canonical publish workflow for Terraform modules used in Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments. It is written as a pragmatic runbook for module authors, reviewers, and release engineers who must balance backward compatibility, security fixes, and the operational impact of changes to on-prem stacks.

Scope and intent:
- Applies to all terraform modules under infra-modules/private/* that are consumed by Private deployment installations (VPC templates, network, ingress, secrets, bootstrap).
- Focuses on versioning rules, how to detect/record breaking changes, the registry publish checklist, and rollback/patch patterns.
- Does not replace policy for non-Terraform artifacts (helm charts, operator images) but includes guidance to coordinate cross-artifact upgrades.

Decision log format (short entries until full audit required):
- Date | Author | Module | Proposed change summary | Compatibility class (patch/minor/major) | Decision | Reason / mitigations | Linked PR / Jira
Example entry:
- 2024-11-02 | Priya Nair | private-network | change: remove deprecated subnet_count input | Compatibility: major | Decision: postpone -> create alias input and deprecation cycle | Reason: breaking removal would force workforce upgrades; mitigation: add subnet_counts_v2, deprecate subnet_count with 2 release cycle | PR: #388 | Jira: INFRA-712

Compatibility classes (decision guide):
- Patch: bug fixes, docs, non-behavioral refactors, default value tightening that is non-breaking when not set. No consumer action expected.
- Minor: additive changes (new outputs, new optional inputs, default behavior that is backwards compatible), performance optimizations that do not change resource identity. Consumers should validate in staging.
- Major: anything that changes resource addresses, removes or renames inputs/outputs, tightens required rollout ordering, or changes semantics in ways that may cause resource replacement. Requires migration plan and 2-phase rollout (deprecate -> adapt -> remove).

Automated compatibility signals (run on PR):
- terraform plan drift detection against a daily snapshot of 50 representative private clusters (nightly test matrix).
- tflint and checkov static checks.
- terraform state import roundtrip smoke test for resources touched by the diff.
- a heuristic that flags changes touching "name", "id", or lifecycle blocks as high-risk.
When a signal is high-risk, the PR must be flagged with label "compatibility:high-risk" and an owner from eng-private-deployments must be assigned.

Publish workflow checklist (pre-publish):
1) Author creates PR with CHANGELOG fragment under modules/<module>/changelog/unreleased.md describing user-facing behavior and migration steps.
2) Add tests: unit test (where applicable), integration smoke that runs plan against a small infra fixture, and state import test.
3) Run compatibility signals (see above) and attach results as artifacts on PR.
4) Reviewer checklist pass (see Reviewer checklist below).
5) Open a release ticket (INFRA-RELEASE-xxx) linking PRs for cross-module coordination.
6) Merge to main only after 2 approvals including one from an owner of the module consumer team.
7) Git tag flow: do not tag manually. A CI release job will create an annotated tag when the release pipeline runs.
8) The release pipeline publishes to the Terraform Registry namespace redwood-inference/private and updates the registry changelog.

Reviewer checklist (short, strikeable):
- Does change affect resource addresses or resource identifiers? If yes, escalate.
- Are any inputs removed or renamed? If yes, ensure deprecation cycle documented and a migration snippet provided.
- Are defaults changed? Document impact and include a QA plan.
- Are outputs removed or format changed? Provide consumer mapping and justification.
- Have automated compatibility signals passed or are failure reasons documented with mitigations?
- Is the module consumer impact matrix updated (list of internal services using module + current pinned version)?
- Are provider version constraints acceptable for on-prem customers (no latest-floating operators)?

Publishing CI details (implementation notes):
- GitHub Actions job: infra-modules/release/publish.yml triggers on main tag create and runs: terraform init (module-only), terraform validate, module-schema-checks, registry-publish script.
- Registry publish script: calls terraform-registry-api with module metadata (CHANGELOG, release_notes.md, example usage), then uploads zipped module contents. Only release-bot token may publish.
- Approval gate: job requires repo-admin + eng-private-deployments approvers in GitHub protected branch settings for the tag create.

Rollback and emergency patching:
- If a published version causes regression in private installs, create an emergency branch: main -> hotfix/<module>-vX.Y.Z-rollback. Apply a patch (semver patch when possible) that restores previous behavior or adds a compatibility shim.
- Release hotfix via the same pipeline but mark the release with tag prerelease: "hotfix" and notify stakeholders.
- In the worst case (live incidents), coordinate a rollout of a pinned module on a per-customer basis via the private deployment operator and provide a configuration overlay to pin module_version.

Deprecation policy and timeline (recommended):
- Announce deprecation in changelog and #private-deployments slack channel with 60 days notice for minor deprecations, 90 days for major deprecations that require changes.
- Follow a 3-stage lifecycle: deprecated -> sunset candidate -> removal. Each stage must be represented in CHANGELOG and release notes.

Migration templates (to include in changelog):
- Short snippet for consumers to adapt provider constraints or input renames. Example: 
  Old: module "network" { source = "redwood-inference/private/network" version = "~> 2.3" subnet_count = 2 }
  New: module "network" { source = "redwood-inference/private/network" version = "~> 3.0" subnet_counts_v2 = [2] // migration: map single value to list and run terraform apply --target=module.network }

Compatibility matrix (author-maintained, keep small):
- Columns: module | last_two_versions | known_consumers | risk_level | notes
- Sample row: private-network | 2.1.7, 2.0.4 | ops-bootstrap, ci-provisioner, enterprise-onprem-template | medium | 2.1.7 introduced new outputs but preserved addresses.

Communication and stakeholders:
- Primary channel: #private-deployments (Slack). Add release announcement with links to CHANGELOG and release ticket.
- Mailing: ops-customer-notify@redwood.ai for customers on committed dedicated/private contracts if change requires them to schedule maintenance.
- Owners: list module owners in module README and in the module metadata file module.metadata.yaml.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide whether to enforce semantic versioning programmatically (CI check) or rely on reviewer discipline. Proposal: add a CI stub that rejects tag pushes which don't match the semver bump heuristic. (owner: Rafael)
- Expand nightly test matrix to include 10 on-prem fixtures that mimic older pinned provider versions.
- Create a small cli tool to generate migration snippets automatically from terraform plan diffs.

Appendix: quick-check commands for authors:
- Run local checks: ./scripts/module-lint.sh modules/<module>
- Run smoke tests: tox -e integration -- modules/<module>/tests/integration
- Generate changelog fragment: ./scripts/new-changelog-entry.sh "modules/<module>" "Short summary"

This document is intentionally compact. Treat it as the single source for routine decisions and the light-weight runbook that should be linked from module READMEs. For heavyweight compatibility disputes or cross-org impact (customer migrations), create a dedicated RFC and attach to the release ticket.

Decision log (recent lines):
- 2025-01-18 | Ethan Brooks | private-bootstrap | change: add kms_key_id optional input (minor) | Decision: approve | Reason: additive; added test coverage in smoke-suite to ensure no address churn | PR: #412 | Jira: INFRA-823
- 2025-01-28 | Ava Chen | private-secrets | change: tighten default lifecycle prevent_destroy = true (major risk) | Decision: staged roll: add flag allow_destroy toggle, announce deprecation and run forced-migration pipeline | PR: #429 | Jira: INFRA-845

If you are editing this doc: append new decision lines at the bottom and keep entries terse. When a decision moves from draft->final, update status and ping channel #private-deployments.
